markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (99%)** · Confident · Read in turn
Single-class conformal set, second-model agreement, and reliable input back this [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 99%, InSitu 1% | Clear separation |
| Conformal set | Benign only | Single class at 90% |
| Reliability / OOD | 100% / 94th percentile | Input not flagged |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Yes | Same top class |
| Similar cases | 2 of 5 Benign | Neighbors split |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 10) · ↑ invasive · Scored below typical; lowers invasive association · Validated
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (regions 1, 9, 11) · ↓ invasive · Scored above typical; points away from invasive · Weak
- **Tumor cell fraction** (regions 0, 1, 10) · context · 83% of nuclei; higher than 99% of reference images · Measured
- **Normal lobules** (region 4) · ↓ invasive · Scored low; spot check failed, 0/20 · Unreliable

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI includes 0 (−0.005 to 0.007); not shown to reflect the classifier. Leans on Unreliable normal lobules.

## Could be wrong if
- 3 of 5 similar cases are InSitu, though the model gives InSitu only 1%.
- The high tumor-nucleus fraction, sampled from 3 regions, is real, not segmentation error.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 1, 9, 11**: Look for atypical cells confined within ducts (weak concept).
2. **Regions 0, 1, 10**: Verify neoplastic nuclei; fraction is high but nuclear size is lowest in reference.
3. **Region 10**: Check for stromal infiltration where that concept scores strongest.
